title: An empty Unassigned group stays in Tech View and accepts a dropped work order
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit (check in Settings > Roles & Permissions > open your role > Work Orders section). The Admin role has both.
  2. Use a desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  3. In the top bar, choose the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty"). Create everything below in this location.
  4. Make sure the location has the technicians this case uses (e.g. "Esther Howard"). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff record is Active, Clockable is on, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member > enter the first and last name (e.g. Esther Howard), role Technician, Clockable on, Active, enrolled at this location > Save.
  5. Create the work orders this case uses and set their lead technician (e.g. S1-702 and S1-644 led by Esther Howard and no work order without a lead (give any unassigned one a lead first)):
    • Work Orders > New Work Order > choose the customer "ZZAUTOTEST Empty Unassigned" (add it with the Add button in the customer box if it does not exist; using it keeps this test's work orders apart from others at the location) and an asset (e.g. unit TRK-118, 2022 Freightliner M2) > Create. Write down the number the build gives the work order (the numbers in this case are examples).
    • On the work order page set Lead Technician (e.g. Esther Howard) and save. Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
  6. Make sure the work orders you will drag have no shift on the Schedule for their lead technician (Schedule > check the technician's row). If a "Clear … scheduled shifts?" prompt appears anyway, click Keep shifts.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. Click the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  3. Click Search and type ZZAUTOTEST Empty Unassigned so only this test's work orders show.
  4. Make sure Assigned to me is off.
  5. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Tech View (in the design its tooltip reads "By Lead Tech").
  6. Read the Unassigned group.
  7. Drag S1-644 from Esther Howard's group onto the Unassigned group and let go.
  8. Read the Unassigned group and Esther Howard's count.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • With no unassigned work, the Unassigned group is still on screen, first, showing "No work orders".
  • S1-644 can be dropped on it: it now sits in Unassigned (Unassigned 1) and Esther Howard's count drops from 2 to 1.
  • When Assigned to me is on, or when nothing matches the filters, Unassigned follows those rules instead (checked in other cases).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10045 (Story 2, Tech View — table grouped by lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S2-N1, read 8 Oct 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-N1: “When Unassigned has no work, the group stays on screen with its empty state as a drop target, except while Assigned to me is enabled (S2-R9), and following S1-N1 when no work orders match the filters.”
